sources.entry: PKVault - Centralized Pokémon storage management & Pokedex app (alternative to Pokémon Home). (Demo) GPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: PKVault is a self-hosted Pokémon storage, save-editing and Pokédex app built on PKHeX, offering a Pokémon Home-like experience that works offline.
summary.what_it_does: PKVault moves Pokémon between game saves, storage banks and boxes, and external PKM files, and can convert Pokémon across generations from Gen 1 up to Pokémon Legends: Z-A. It lets you edit moves, EVs and nicknames, evolve trade-based Pokémon, and move items between saves, inventories and held items. Every save action is preceded by a backup, and backups can be listed and restored. A centralized Pokédex built from all listed saves supports forms, genders, several filters, and living and shiny dex views. Save files are found through configurable paths and globs. The README says it is distributed as desktop builds for Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, a Flatpak, and a Docker image.
use_cases: manage Pokémon storage across multiple game saves
build a living or shiny Pokédex
edit Pokémon moves, EVs and nicknames
back up and restore Pokémon save files
self-host a Pokémon Home alternative in a homelab
how_to_run: Or use the docker-compose.yml example from the README with the ghcr.io/chnapy/pkvault image
Windows: run PKVault.exe from the releases page
Linux and SteamDeck: install from Flathub (recommended) or use a Linux build from releases
Android: install pkvault.apk from releases, allowing installs from unknown sources
macOS: unzip the .app.zip and open PKVault.app, then allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security
notable: Built on the PKHeX core library for save parsing and Pokémon conversion
Runs as a Docker image on Linux x86_64 and ARM, including Raspberry Pi
Works fully offline; suggests syncthing or similar tools for syncing data between devices
Automatic backups before any save change, with restore support
caveats: The README says online features are out of project scope; device sync must be handled by third-party tools
The macOS build is not notarized, so Gatekeeper requires a manual override
Android requires allowing installs from unknown sources
